findings.finding: The iptables rule blocking 169.254.169.254 for non-bot container networks — the containment control that justifies raising the hop limit — is placed in `infra/scripts/` with no specified persistence mechanism. Nothing in the plan ensures the rule survives a host reboot, a `docker compose down && up`, or an autodeploy cycle. A reboot clears iptables state on AL2023 unless persisted via a systemd unit (e.g. `iptables-restore`), cloud-init, or a host service; at that point the widened hop limit hands the node role to every container on the box, directly violating the security posture claimed in ADR 0046.
findings.location: Scope section — `infra/scripts/` bullet; Testing section — negative-control AC; Acceptance Criteria — AC[c]
scenarios: Host reboots (e.g. after a kernel patch or AWS stop/start): iptables rules are cleared, all containers can reach IMDS with hop-limit 2
Autodeploy restarts docker-compose: if the rule lives only in a script run once at boot, it may not be re-applied
An operator running `compose-up.sh` on a fresh instance does not automatically re-install the rule unless the script explicitly calls the iptables setup
findings.suggested_fix: Add an `ExecStartPre` in a new systemd unit file (e.g. `rebar-imds-guard.service`) that runs the iptables rule before docker.service starts, and install it via the existing `install-autodeploy.sh` pattern. Reference the unit in the Scope section and add a step to the runbook verifying the rule survives `systemctl reboot`.
